+
Architecture research · 26 September 2026
+

Pokémon Emerald × JEV

+

What must change to move the Jev Plays Pokémon Red harness onto Emerald with mGBA—and, crucially, what should not change.

+

The JEV request/choice protocol is reusable. The substantial work is building the Emerald-specific boundary that turns mGBA’s raw bytes and key masks into safe, typed decisions.

+

  • State layers
  • How JEV decides

+
+ +
+

The core: five boundaries, one narrow decision choke point

+
+

1. mGBA + Lua

raw machine state
  • bus / memory-domain reads
  • frame count and callback timing
  • GBA 10-key bitmask
  • save/load state; screenshot

No Pokémon concepts here.

→
+

2. Emerald profile decoder

typed game state
  • read ROM-profile globals and dereference SaveBlock pointers
  • decode party, bag, flags, map, objects, battle, menu, text
  • recognize stable / input-ready boundaries

Owns version-specific addresses, text encoding and layouts.

+

3. Classifier + legal branch

decision state

This is the protective adapter around JEV.

4. JEV policy

typed choice
  • input: { state, questions }
  • question: choice, score, or boolean
  • output: option ID, optionally probabilities

It ranks the supplied alternatives; it does not manipulate RAM or press buttons.

→
+

5. Executor + verifier

controller effect
  • validate selected ID
  • compile intent into cursor-relative buttons and frame holds
  • observe expected outcome; log / checkpoint / safely retry

The game sees only normal controller input.

Feeds the next stable decision point.

+
+

Do not wire JEV directly to mGBA. Raw addresses are ROM-version details; raw button sequences are timing-sensitive. The bridge should accept only a validated semantic action (for example, use_move:2) and be solely responsible for the button choreography.

+
+ +
+

“Each possible state” — the useful answer is layered

+

A complete enumeration of Pokémon’s machine states is astronomically large. The harness instead gives each layer a different, finite job. “Possible” below means the state families the bridge must represent, not every numeric value or every story permutation.

+ + + + + + +
LayerPossible states / contentsWho creates itWhat JEV receives?
Emulator snapshotGBA CPU/registers; ROM; BIOS; EWRAM, IWRAM, MMIO, VRAM, palette and OAM; framebuffer; current frame; key mask; full save state.mGBANo
Emerald decoded stateROM profile identity; pointers and SaveBlocks; game callback/task/script lock; map group/number, position, facing, motion; object events; party/PC/bag/money; flags/vars; dialog/menu/cursor; battle participants, status, PP, side conditions, phase and legal UI state.Profile decoderUsually no—only a projection

+

Red harness’s actual mode classifier

It recognizes five modes: battle, dialog, overworld, busy, and boot. “Busy” means wait rather than call JEV—important because cutscenes and transitions can ignore input.

Emerald’s essential extra distinction

In Emerald, inBattle alone is insufficient. Battle controller buffers and execution flags can mean animation or a selection protocol is still in progress. Prompt only when the player can actually make the relevant choice.

+
+ +
+

How state gets into JEV, and how the decision is made

+

What crosses the boundary

The JEV client sends structured JSON:

{
+  state: { objective, party, bag, location, recentDialog,
+           battle: { enemy, active, ... } },
+  questions: {
+    decision: { type: "choice", instructions: "...",
+                criteria: { "Use Ember": "Fire; 25 PP; ...",
+                            "Switch to X": "..." } }
+  }
+}

The model returns a selected key (and may return probabilities). It does not get arbitrary RAM, symbols, coordinates to invent, or a button API.

What “JEV decides” actually means

JEV chooses the best supplied option based on the typed state and option descriptions. The real JEV model’s internal scoring is external and not exposed by this repository.

The harness decision logic remains very substantial: it computes legal options and facts, filters impossible actions, caches/throttles calls, detects lack of progress, may sample from model probabilities to escape loops, and can restore a checkpoint as a last resort.

+

Decision surfaces to port

+ + + + + +
SituationSemantic choices JEV may receiveHarness-provided facts / mechanics
OverworldFocus: progress, heal, train, catch, shop, explore, team; then reachable warp/exit/NPC/sign/grass/item/field-move target.Collision and route graph, A* path, objective distance, availability, visited/blocked history.

The bundled mock backend is not the real model: it scores positive/negative words in option descriptions, adds noise, softmaxes, then takes the highest score. It is valuable only as a protocol/offline test double.

+

+

+

Engineering-surface estimate: roughly 2–4× the Red port, not a simple line-for-line conversion. This is an informed sizing judgment from the inspected code, not a measured schedule. The typed JEV client stays close to unchanged; the game adapter and semantic extraction grow materially.

Use one checksum-verified US Emerald v1.0 profile and a user-local checkpoint at Birch’s starter decision. Repository claims below were read from the linked source. The local workspace presently contains the design plan, not an executable Emerald bridge; its claims are therefore proposal, not implementation evidence.

content.text:
Yes—clone `jev-pokemon` as the starting point. That is the sensible route.

But it is not “swap in an Emerald ROM.” The Red harness is tightly coupled to:

- `serverboy` / Game Boy emulation
- Red’s RAM symbols, 44-byte party layout, tilemap/font, maps, collisions, and Gen-1 battle math
- Red-specific menus and milestones

Those are embedded in its emulator and game layers. The typed JEV protocol is already generic: `{ state, questions } → selected option key`, so retain `src/jev/` nearly intact and preserve the agent/logging/checkpoint architecture. [JEV types](https://github.com/christianmat/jev-pokemon/blob/dd8b18cd97923cdfc547e9c1acecfe4fb831c442/src/jev/types.ts#L3-L28)

Practical split:

| Reuse | Replace |
|---|---|
| JEV client, throttling, logs, cache, choice interface | Emulator adapter → mGBA |
| Agent loop structure, checkpoint/loop protection | RAM/ROM/text/map/battle decoders |
| Semantic-action → controller-input pattern | Emerald menus, routing, and battle legality |

So: clone it, then make an `emerald` branch and replace `src/emu/` and most of `src/game/` first. For a starter-to-first-battle proof, that is quite feasible; full-world play is the larger project.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: Replacement.md
+# What must be replaced to port `jev-pokemon` from Red to Emerald
+
+## Decision
+
+Forking `christianmat/jev-pokemon` is a good way to preserve its JEV policy
+protocol, logging, and control-loop shape. It is **not** a ROM swap or a
+small emulator adapter change. The original harness has Pokémon Red / Game
+Boy assumptions throughout its emulator, RAM decoder, ROM parser, text/menu
+reader, pathfinder, battle facts, and milestones.
+
+The safe boundary remains:
+
+```text
+mGBA raw bytes + frames + GBA keys
+  -> Emerald ROM-profile decoder
+  -> typed, stable GameState
+  -> branch classifier + finite LegalAction[]
+  -> JEV selected action ID
+  -> validated GBA input sequence
+  -> observed outcome / replay log
+```
+
+JEV must receive neither raw addresses nor raw key presses.
+
+## Reuse with little or no semantic change
+
+| Original area | Why it survives | Required adaptation |
+|---|---|---|
+| `src/jev/types.ts` | It defines a generic JSON request: state plus choice/score/boolean questions, and a typed answer. | Rename only if desired; retain option IDs as the action boundary. |
+| `src/jev/client.ts` | Caching, throttling, retries, call logs, and probability sampling do not depend on Pokémon generation. | Make idle-frame ticking call the new mGBA adapter. |
+| `src/jev/gateway.ts` | It serializes the generic typed request to JEV. | Retain; test against recorded responses. |
+| Logging/checkpoint/replay idea | Decision record, state fingerprint, legal actions, compiled input, and observed result remain valuable. | Define a versioned Emerald record schema. |
+| Agent-loop architecture | `observe -> classify -> choose -> execute -> verify` is the right decomposition. | Do not preserve Red's actual mode predicates. |
+
+## Replace outright
+
+| Original area | Red-specific assumption | Emerald replacement |
+|---|---|---|
+| `src/emu/emulator.ts` | In-process `serverboy` Game Boy core, direct JavaScript memory array, 8 buttons. | mGBA Lua bridge + local controller protocol. Use GBA key masks, frame stepping, state files, and read-only bus/domain telemetry. |
+| `src/game/symbols.ts` | Generated `pokered` symbols and fixed locations. | `EmeraldRomProfile`: ROM SHA-256, known globals, struct offsets, text/table metadata, and startup invariants. |
+| `src/game/state.ts` | Red WRAM field names, 44-byte Gen-1 party entries, fixed tile map and menu registers. | Decoder for Emerald runtime state, SaveBlock pointers, Gen-3 Pokémon structures, battle controller state, menu/text/cursor state, scripts and input lock. |
+| `src/game/rom.ts` | Red ROM banks, map headers, type chart, species/move/item tables and object encodings. | Emerald data reader, preferably derived from an exact profile / decomp symbols for a validated target build. |
+| `src/game/text.ts` and menu decoding | Red font, 20×18 tile map and cursor glyph conventions. | Emerald character map and UI-specific readers. Use RAM telemetry first; use screenshots only to corroborate visible prompts. |
+| `src/game/world.ts`, `regions.ts` | Red collision and map graph formats. | Emerald map-group/event/connection/object/collision model, with dynamic scripts and avatar readiness. |
+| `src/agent/battle.ts` | Gen-1 damage, catch, physical/special, Safari, and menu mechanics. | Emerald legal-action builder. It must support Gen-3 mechanics and branch explicitly for singles, doubles, targets, forced switches, item restrictions and special battles. |
+| `src/knowledge/milestones.ts` | Red event flags and story locations. | Emerald goals and validated event-flag predicates. |
+
+## Adapt cautiously
+
+| Area | What changes |
+|---|---|
+| Mode classifier | Preserve the idea of `boot`, `busy`, `overworld`, `dialog/menu`, and `battle`, but base it on Emerald callbacks/tasks/scripts, input lock, menu state and battle controller requests—not only an in-battle byte. |
+| Overworld decisions | Retain semantic candidate selection, but rebuild candidate generation and path execution around Emerald maps and runtime objects. Scripts may ignore keys or move the avatar. |
+| Menu executor | Retain cursor-relative execution and postcondition checks. Re-measure all frame holds/releases; never assume Red timings or menu layout. |
+| Battle facts | Continue giving JEV legal moves and explanatory facts. Calculate only facts whose Emerald mechanic has been implemented and tested; unknown legality is a reason to withhold an action, not guess. |
+| Save states | Retain checkpoint/retry concept but treat mGBA states as opaque, versioned emulator artifacts. Keep ROMs and saves user-local. |
+
+## Emerald-specific risks that invalidate a “small adaptation” estimate
+
+1. **The hardware/emulator boundary changes.** mGBA Lua provides raw reads,
+   key masks, frame control, callbacks, screenshots and save states; it does
+   not provide Pokémon state or a JEV integration. A bridge protocol is new
+   production code.
+2. **Addresses require a profile.** Emerald's SaveBlocks are pointer-based and
+   relocated. A decoder must locate profile-known pointer globals before it
+   reads struct offsets; hard-coding a single observed EWRAM address is unsafe.
+3. **Gen-3 Pokémon data is harder.** Persistent Pokémon use encrypted,
+   personality-selected substructures. Party and battle copies are related but
+   not interchangeable.
+4. **A frame is not a choice boundary.** Text printing, animation, scripts,
+   map loads and battle-controller sequences span variable frames. The bridge
+   needs readiness predicates and action verifiers.
+5. **Battle legality is broader.** A full harness must handle doubles,
+   target selection, forced replacements, trapping, item restrictions,
+   special encounters and UI branches. The first proof should intentionally
+   omit most of that surface.
+6. **World routing is a new parser.** Emerald map groups, events, dynamic
+   objects and scripts make Red's region graph non-portable.
+
+## Minimal proof that proves the architecture
+
+Target one checksum-verified US Emerald v1.0 ROM profile and a user-local
+checkpoint at Professor Birch's starter decision.
+
+1. Lua bridge proves mGBA capabilities at startup and serves requests from a
+   local controller without blocking frame callbacks.
+2. Decoder recognizes the starter prompt, three legal starter options, and
+   current cursor.
+3. JEV receives only those three semantic options and selects one.
+4. Executor moves from the observed cursor, presses GBA keys, and verifies the
+   selected starter entered the party.
+5. Decoder recognizes the first forced battle and emits only legal move actions.
+6. Executor verifies battle victory, writing a replayable record for each
+   decision.
+
+This slice establishes the bridge, profile, typed policy, input compiler, and
+verifier. It does **not** establish full overworld routing, general menus, or
+the complete Gen-3 battle matrix.
+
+## Gates before expanding scope
+
+- Reject ROM hashes not explicitly profiled.
+- Assert pointer ranges and decoded-state invariants before every decision.
+- Never write game RAM in the harness; use only normal controller input.
+- Ask JEV only at a stable, classified decision boundary.
+- Reject a JEV answer not present in the current legal action set.
+- Verify each action's expected postcondition before the next decision.
+- Record enough data to replay failures without calling JEV again.
+
+## Sources
+
+- `https://github.com/christianmat/jev-pokemon` at commit

Yes—PyBoyAdvance is architecturally much closer to how JEV Plays Pokémon Red works.

Both use an in-process loop:

```text
load ROM → read emulator memory → decode game state
→ ask JEV for a legal choice → press buttons → advance frames
→ read the result
```

The Red harness’s ServerBoy adapter already does direct memory access, button presses, frame stepping, and screen reads. [Red adapter](https://github.com/christianmat/jev-pokemon/blob/dd8b18cd97923cdfc547e9c1acecfe4fb831c442/src/emu/emulator.ts#L40-L70) PyBoyAdvance offers the GBA equivalents directly in Python: `frame`, `press_key`, `release_key`, memory, and an RGB framebuffer. [PyBoyAdvance API](https://github.com/williamckha/PyBoyAdvance/blob/f2ff0ec6657964b9fffdbbdeeecee7043385c2a8/pyboy_advance/pyboy_advance.py#L91-L131)

So yes: for a prototype, it lets us copy the Red harness’s overall shape much more directly than mGBA.

The non-transferable part is still the game adapter: Red’s state reader assumes Red RAM symbols and 44-byte Gen-1 Pokémon records; Emerald needs new Gen-3 state, battle, menu, and map decoding. PyBoyAdvance makes the emulator boundary easier—not Emerald semantics free.
